title: Point-of-Care Capillary Toe-to-Finger Lactate Gradient During Early Emergency Department Sepsis Resuscitation
authors_line: Nadia Karim, MD; Owen Brooks, RN, MSN
affiliations_line: Institutional affiliation not specified in source abstract (Synthetic Pilot Submission)

items.title: Clinical Context
paragraphs: Macrohemodynamic stabilization during early septic shock resuscitation can mask persistent peripheral microcirculatory hypoperfusion.
bullets: Objective: Test whether bedside capillary toe-to-finger lactate gradient (ΔLac) at 2 hours predicts 72-hour vasopressor dependency.

items.title: Pilot Study Design (N = 164)
bullets: Setting & Cohort: Prospective single-ED observational pilot study of N = 164 adults with suspected septic shock.
Measurement: Paired fingertip and hallux point-of-care capillary lactate sampled at baseline (0 h) and 2 hours post-crystalloid resuscitation.
Pre-specified Exposure Threshold: 2-hour ΔLac ≥ 1.2 mmol/L (n = 58, 35.4%) vs. ΔLac < 1.2 mmol/L (n = 106, 64.6%).

items.title: Source Scope & Transparency Note
paragraphs: Designed strictly from the accepted pilot abstract. Multivariable adjusted models, secondary organ-dysfunction endpoints, and formal limitation statements were not reported in the abstract and were intentionally omitted without fabrication.

items.title: Principal Pilot Finding
paragraphs: Patients with persistent 2-hour capillary ΔLac ≥ 1.2 mmol/L experienced nearly threefold higher 72-hour vasopressor dependency (62.1% vs. 21.7%).

items.title: 72-Hour Vasopressor Dependency by 2-Hour ΔLac
items.caption: Figure 1. Observed 72-hour vasopressor dependency across 2-hour capillary lactate gradient strata (N = 164; exact binomial proportions).

items.title: Conclusions & Next Steps
paragraphs: Bedside 2-hour capillary toe-to-finger lactate gradient rapidly identifies occult microcirculatory failure during initial ED sepsis resuscitation and warrants prospective multicenter validation.
